# 2014A Question 15 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Indicate**]{.task-verb} the sequence of the physiological changes to the fetal circulation at birth and [**briefly describe**]{.task-verb} the mechanisms that account for these changes.
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Indicate**]{.task-verb} the sequence from placental separation and first breaths to closure of the fetal shunts. [**Briefly describe**]{.task-verb} the mechanisms in a table, including the timing of functional and anatomical changes.

::: {.structure-table}
| Event or Structure | Circulatory Change | Mechanism | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Placental Separation | | | |
| First Breaths and Vascular Resistance | | | |
| Foramen Ovale | | | |
| Ductus Arteriosus | | | |
| Ductus Venosus | | | |
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**40.8%** of candidates achieved a pass in this question

Main Points expected for a pass:

- removal of the placenta and consequences of this.

- reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance.

- increase in systemic vascular resistance.

- closure of ductus venosus, foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus.

- discussion of the mechanisms for these changes.

Additional points could be gained for:

- time scales of changes.

- cellular mechanisms of changes.

- clinical significance.

- noting that these changes are reversible for varying amounts of time.

Common problems:

- illegible handwriting

- poor layout and structure and evidence of poor time management

- too much time spent on outlining normal fetal circulation.

- time wasted drawing diagrams.

- confusion as to where shunts were located and the role of prostaglandins.

- the main reason for failing this question was insufficient core knowledge
:::
